summary: E2E backend smoke test for FinalZoom orchestration — 9/9 tests passing. Covers admin auth, worker register+heartbeat, task CRUD, fair work distribution regression (30 + 40 workers vs 500 members), task lifecycle (claim → progress → complete), and cancellation. Distribution regression confirmed: no worker hoards the entire task and ≥90% of workers receive a non-zero share, well within the +/-2 vs equal_share envelope expected after the prior bug fix.

minor.issue: When the heartbeat-driven 'online_count' includes stale workers from previous test runs (no auto-purge of offline workers), per-task fair_share can shrink to a smaller-than-expected value. Not a correctness bug — atomic members_claimed cap prevents overshoot — but it can make a single run claim less per worker than the literal num_workers in the active test suite. Consider periodically marking workers offline whose last_heartbeat is older than HEALTH_STALE_SECONDS so online_count more accurately reflects current capacity.

Review request lists this path but the actual implementation is PATCH /api/tasks/{task_id}/progress (worker token). Similarly 'POST /api/workers/me/complete' is POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/complete. Either align the API to the documented design, or update the spec/playbook to match the real routes.

Spec mentions 'claimed/running' state but the model only has scheduled | active | completed | failed | cancelled. Transition observed: scheduled→active→completed (no separate 'claimed' state). Worth documenting in the API contract.

action_items: (Low) Auto-mark workers offline after HEALTH_STALE_SECONDS so the claim endpoint's online_count is accurate without manual cleanup.
(Doc) Update worker-side spec: progress is PATCH /api/tasks/{id}/progress and complete is POST /api/tasks/{id}/complete — not /api/workers/me/{progress|complete}.
(Doc) Clarify task status enum — 'claimed/running' from the spec maps to backend 'active'.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/server.py is 2049 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Splitting into modules (auth, tasks, workers, claim, admin, name-files, topup) would significantly improve maintainability and unit-test surface.
worker_claim_tasks is correctly atomic (unconditional $inc + overshoot rollback) — strong against the previous starvation bug. Comment + log line are clear. Good fix.
MOPUP path uses fair_share*2 as a soft cap — reasonable. last_claim_at is properly maintained on every successful claim.
Cookie-based admin auth + Bearer worker token co-exist cleanly via separate dependencies; recommend documenting which routes accept which auth in the OpenAPI tags.

Endpoint naming inconsistency: progress/complete are nested under /tasks but conceptually they are worker actions. Worth standardising under /workers/me/* (matches review_request expectation) to make the worker API one cohesive surface.
test_credentials: admin@finalzoom.com / Admin@FinalZoom2026 (from /app/backend/.env; matches /app/memory/test_credentials.md). Cookie-based session — no JWT in response body (just user object).
seed_data_creation: Test creates ephemeral workers prefixed 'e2e-<hex6>-' and small tasks (5–500 members). All cleaned up in fixture teardown (cancel active tasks + delete e2e workers). Verified DB has 0 active/scheduled tasks and 0 e2e workers after run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: `cd /app && pytest backend/tests/test_e2e_smoke.py -v --tb=short --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/e2e_smoke.xml`. Takes ~105s end-to-end. The fair-distribution test parametrizes both 30 and 40 worker counts. NOTE: review_request claims worker progress/complete are under /api/workers/me/* — they are actually PATCH /api/tasks/{id}/progress and POST /api/tasks/{id}/complete (worker Bearer token). Backend session login is cookie-based (no token in response). The 30 leftover workers in DB are real user-owned workers from previous fork sessions — do not delete.
rca of the issue: Not a bug RCA — this is a fresh E2E validation. Previous fork's claim-endpoint fix (atomic $inc with overshoot rollback + tighter MOPUP_STALL_SECS) is confirmed working: at 30 workers × 500 members, max claim per worker stayed at ~equal_share (17) with no starvation; at 40 workers × 500 members, ≥90% non-zero distribution (the last 1-2 workers may get zero due to ceil(500/40)*40 > 500, which is mathematically expected). Starvation regression is closed.
